### What does this PR do?

On the V1 trainer (the `main_ppo` default), `algorithm.adv_estimator=gdpo` fails on the first advantage step. `_compute_advantage` fetches only `uid`, `response_mask`, `rm_scores` and the log-prob/value fields, so the `DataProto` handed to `compute_advantage` has:

- no reward components: v0 puts each `reward_extra_info` key into `non_tensor_batch`, and V1 never does;
- no `prompts` / `attention_mask`, which `compute_gdpo_outcome_advantage` uses to find each response's last token.

The estimator raises `KeyError: 'prompts'`, and past that its `GDPO reward key ... not found in non_tensor_batch` assertion.

This PR fetches the `gdpo_reward_keys` components and gives the estimator what it needs to place them, so V1 GDPO matches v0.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here:
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+gdpo
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+gdpo_reward_keys
  - https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+%22v1+_compute_advantage%22
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

Why this is not a duplicate:

- #5613, #6497 and #7965 change `compute_gdpo_outcome_advantage` in `core_algos.py`. None of them touch the V1 trainer, and on V1 the estimator fails before it reaches their code paths.
- #7473 passes `non_tensor_batch` to estimators in the v0 `ray_trainer.py` only.
- #7497 (CoDaPO) also forwards `reward_extra_info` into the V1 advantage batch, for its own estimator. That covers half of this: GDPO would still raise `KeyError: 'prompts'`, and a colocated reward model writes the components as their own fields rather than in `extra_fields`. Whichever lands first, I will rebase the other onto it.

### Test

New `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_gdpo_on_cpu.py` runs `_compute_advantage` against an in-memory TransferQueue and compares the V1 advantages token by token with v0's `compute_advantage` on the same rewards, for both the streaming reward path (`extra_fields`) and a colocated reward model (per-key fields).

```bash
pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_gdpo_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_compute_reward_colocate_on_cpu.py
```

- main: both new cases fail with `KeyError: 'key "prompts" not found in TensorDict ...'`.
- this PR: 23 passed.

I have not run GDPO end to end on GPU for this change; the CPU test checks V1 against v0 directly.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`:

- `_compute_advantage`: for GDPO, select `extra_fields` (streaming reward path) or the `gdpo_reward_keys` fields (colocated reward model, which writes each reward extra key as its own field), and put the components into `non_tensor_batch`.
- Give the estimator an empty `prompts` and an `attention_mask` covering each full response. GDPO only uses them to find the last response token, so this places each component exactly where v0 does, tool tokens included (they are in v0's attention mask too).
- `_pop_gdpo_rewards`: a small helper that reads the components from either layout. Keys missing from any sample are left out, so the estimator's existing assertion still reports them.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_gdpo_on_cpu.py` is picked up by the CPU unit test workflow.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). (If not accessible, please try [the Feishu group (飞书群)](https://applink.larkoffice.com/client/chat/chatter/add_by_link?link_token=772jd4f1-cd91-441e-a820-498c6614126a).)

**AI assistance:** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude), which found the bug in a V0/V1 trainer comparison, wrote the fix and test, and ran the commands above.

- #7473 passes `non_tensor_batch` to estimators in the v0 `ray_trainer.py` only.
- #7497 (CoDaPO) also forwards `reward_extra_info` into the V1 advantage batch, for its own estimator. That covers half of this: GDPO would still raise `KeyError: 'prompts'`, and a colocated reward model writes the components as their own fields rather than in `extra_fields`. Whichever lands first, I will rebase the other onto it.

### Test

New `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_gdpo_on_cpu.py` runs `_compute_advantage` against an in-memory TransferQueue and compares the V1 advantages token by token with v0's `compute_advantage` on the same rewards, for both the streaming reward path (`extra_fields`) and a colocated reward model (per-key fields).

```bash
pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_gdpo_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_compute_reward_colocate_on_cpu.py
```

- main: both new cases fail with `KeyError: 'key "prompts" not found in TensorDict ...'`.
- this PR: 23 passed.

I have not run GDPO end to end on GPU for this change; the CPU test checks V1 against v0 directly.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`:

- `_compute_advantage`: for GDPO, select `extra_fields` (streaming reward path) or the `gdpo_reward_keys` fields (colocated reward model, which writes each reward extra key as its own field), and put the components into `non_tensor_batch`.
- Give the estimator an empty `prompts` and an `attention_mask` covering each full response. GDPO only uses them to find the last response token, so this places each component exactly where v0 does, tool tokens included (they are in v0's attention mask too).
- `_pop_gdpo_rewards`: a small helper that reads the components from either layout. Keys missing from any sample are left out, so the estimator's existing assertion still reports them.

+GDPO_KEYS = ["acc", "fmt"]
+
+
+class _Row(NamedTuple):
+    uid: int
+    session: int
+    index: int
+    prompt_len: int
+    response_len: int
+    rewards: tuple[float, float]
+
+
+# One output per session: two prompts (uids), rollout.n = 2 sessions each.
+SINGLE_OUTPUT_ROWS = [
+    _Row(0, 0, 0, 3, 3, (1.0, 0.5)),
+    _Row(0, 1, 0, 2, 2, (0.0, 1.0)),
+    _Row(1, 0, 0, 4, 4, (0.0, 1.0)),
+    _Row(1, 1, 0, 1, 1, (1.0, 0.0)),
+]
+# Session (0, 0) also emits an intermediate output, which the agent loop gives the final output's rewards.
+MULTI_OUTPUT_ROWS = [
+    _Row(0, 0, 0, 2, 5, (1.0, 0.5)),
+    _Row(0, 0, 1, 3, 3, (1.0, 0.5)),
+    *SINGLE_OUTPUT_ROWS[1:],
+]
+
+
+class _StubTrainer(PPOTrainer):
+    def on_step_end(self):
+        pass
+
+    def on_sample_end(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class _FakeTQ:
+    """In-memory stand-in for the TransferQueue key-value API used by the trainer."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fields: dict):
+        self.store = dict(fields)
+
+    def kv_batch_get(self, keys, partition_id, select_fields):
+        return tu.get_tensordict({k: self.store[k] for k in select_fields if k in self.store})
+
+    def kv_batch_put(self, keys, partition_id, fields):
+        for k in fields.keys():
+            self.store[k] = fields[k]
+        return SimpleNamespace(keys=keys, partition_id=partition_id, extra_info={})
+
+
+class _Batch(SimpleNamespace):
+    def __len__(self):
+        return len(self.keys)
+
+
+def _nested(rows):
+    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(rows, layout=torch.jagged)
+
+
+def _make_trainer(colocated_reward: bool):
+    trainer = _StubTrainer.__new__(_StubTrainer)
+    trainer.config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "algorithm": {
+                "adv_estimator": "gdpo",
+                "gdpo_reward_keys": GDPO_KEYS,
+                "gamma": 1.0,
+                "lam": 1.0,
+                "use_kl_in_reward": False,
+                "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo": True,
+                "rollout_correction": None,
+            },
+            "actor_rollout_ref": {"rollout": {"n": 2}},
+        }
+    )
+    trainer.reward_loop_manager = SimpleNamespace(
+        reward_loop_worker_handles=None if colocated_reward else [MagicMock()]
+    )
+    return trainer
+
+
+def _key(row: _Row) -> str:
+    return f"{row.uid}_{row.session}_{row.index}"
+
+
+def _rm_scores(rows):
+    scores = []
+    for row in rows:
+        score = torch.zeros(row.response_len)
+        score[-1] = sum(row.rewards)
+        scores.append(score)
+    return scores
+
+
+def _fake_tq(rows, colocated_reward: bool):
+    fields = {
+        "uid": torch.tensor([row.uid for row in rows]),
+        "response_mask": _nested([torch.ones(row.response_len, dtype=torch.long) for row in rows]),
+        "rm_scores": _nested(_rm_scores(rows)),
+    }
+    if colocated_reward:
+        fields.update({key: np.array([row.rewards[k] for row in rows]) for k, key in enumerate(GDPO_KEYS)})
+    else:
+        fields["extra_fields"] = [
+            {"reward_extra_info": {key: row.rewards[k] for k, key in enumerate(GDPO_KEYS)}} for row in rows
+        ]
+    return _FakeTQ(fields)
+
+
+def _v0_advantages(rows):
+    """GDPO advantages from the v0 trainer's padded [prompt | response] layout, which holds one
+    output per session: the session's final one. Every output of a session gets that advantage."""
+    final = {}
+    for row in rows:
+        if (row.uid, row.session) not in final or final[(row.uid, row.session)].index < row.index:
+            final[(row.uid, row.session)] = row
+    finals = list(final.values())
+    max_prompt = max(row.prompt_len for row in finals)
+    max_response = max(row.response_len for row in finals)
+    prompts = torch.zeros(len(finals), max_prompt, dtype=torch.long)
+    attention_mask = torch.zeros(len(finals), max_prompt + max_response, dtype=torch.long)
+    response_mask = torch.zeros(len(finals), max_response, dtype=torch.long)
+    token_level_rewards = torch.zeros(len(finals), max_response)
+    for i, (row, score) in enumerate(zip(finals, _rm_scores(finals), strict=True)):
+        attention_mask[i, max_prompt - row.prompt_len : max_prompt + row.response_len] = 1
+        response_mask[i, : row.response_len] = 1
+        token_level_rewards[i, : row.response_len] = score
+    data = DataProto.from_dict(
+        tensors={
+            "prompts": prompts,
+            "attention_mask": attention_mask,
+            "response_mask": response_mask,
+            "token_level_rewards": token_level_rewards,
+        },
+        non_tensors={
+            "uid": np.array([row.uid for row in finals], dtype=object),
+            **{key: np.array([row.rewards[k] for row in finals]) for k, key in enumerate(GDPO_KEYS)},
+        },
+    )
+    config = OmegaConf.create({"gdpo_reward_keys": GDPO_KEYS})
+    data = compute_advantage(data, adv_estimator="gdpo", num_repeat=2, config=config)
+    per_session = {(row.uid, row.session): data.batch["advantages"][i, 0] for i, row in enumerate(finals)}
+    return [per_session[(row.uid, row.session)].expand(row.response_len) for row in rows]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [SINGLE_OUTPUT_ROWS, MULTI_OUTPUT_ROWS], ids=["single_output", "multi_output"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("colocated_reward", [False, True])
+def test_v1_gdpo_matches_v0(monkeypatch, rows, colocated_reward):
+    fake_tq = _fake_tq(rows, colocated_reward)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(trainer_base, "tq", fake_tq)
+    trainer = _make_trainer(colocated_reward)
+    batch = _Batch(keys=[_key(row) for row in rows], partition_id="train", extra_info={})
+
+    trainer._compute_advantage(batch, metrics={})
+
+    advantages = fake_tq.store["advantages"].unbind()
+    expected = _v0_advantages(rows)
+    # GDPO gives each sample a non-trivial advantage here, so a zero or mismatched result would fail.
+    assert all(row.abs().sum() > 0 for row in expected)
+    for actual_row, expected_row in zip(advantages, expected, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_row, expected_row)

+    @staticmethod
+    def _pop_gdpo_rewards(data: TensorDict, gdpo_reward_keys: list[str]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:

+        def _to_list(values) -> list:

+        ]
+        return {

+            for key in gdpo_reward_keys
+            if all(key in info for info in reward_extra_infos)
+        }
+

         required_multiple = dp_size

+        gdpo_reward_keys = None

+            # A colocated reward model writes each reward extra key as its own field; the streaming reward
+            # path keeps them in each sample's extra_fields["reward_extra_info"].
+            if self.reward_loop_manager.reward_loop_worker_handles is None:

         data = tq.kv_batch_get(keys=batch.keys, partition_id=batch.partition_id, select_fields=fields)

+        gdpo_rewards = None
+        if gdpo_reward_keys is not None:

         data = DataProto(batch=data.to_padded_tensor())
         data.batch["token_level_scores"] = data.batch["rm_scores"]
         data.non_tensor_batch["uid"] = np.array(data.batch.pop("uid").tolist(), dtype=object)
+        if gdpo_rewards is not None:
